approval_context: Owner confirmed the preview visual direction for Otis and explicitly requested implementation in the actual V6B pixel pipeline. The original Theodore body, suit, backpack, motion and pivot must remain exact. Approved helmet silhouette: compact flat-top turquoise mechanical housing with two short red horns, opaque horizontal chrome visor without visible eyes/face, large circular side cap, short rotating front muzzle and plain square teal back. Previous transparent-goggles iteration was rejected and must not be presented as approved.
reusable_insights: For a body-preserving variation, directly modify the source actor's true 64x112 RGBA frame at the head only; assert Theodore's lower body and grounded feet are pixel-for-pixel identical.

Pixel preview screenshots must not be mistaken for game-ready source assets: implement the owner-approved design in the actual per-actor generator and regenerate original four-way frame sets using the established catalog build.

A fully opaque helmet should not expose fake facial-expression presets; metal pixels must cover underlying eyes on both front directions and the face preview database must report zero visible expressions.

For a helmet with a protruding mechanical muzzle, rotate its cage in the actual authored PNG frames and omit the muzzle entirely on the back, while preserving a flat-topped rear square and constrained 64x112 silhouette.
promotion_rationale: The horned helmet and rotating snout are an intentionally actor-specific illustrated part; reuse Theodore source motions without altering existing approved generators, and keep shared motion/bone code unchanged.
compatibility: Theodore's original renderer, source images, grounded body motions and animation timings are unchanged. Otis remains an independent HELMETED actor. Game's encrypted production world is not altered.
limitations: This integrates the approved static helmet design and available Theodore-based source motion frames, not a newly skinned automatic bone rig or an NPC spawned in the encrypted game.
